first.rationale: I intend to test onboarding simplification because completion and activation are both deteriorating, and the inherited evidence suggests shorter onboarding improves time-to-value while in-product activation messaging improves early engagement. I would verify both records before committing, run a guarded test, and measure qualified revenue and retention—not just completion or activation—to avoid optimizing shallow activity. Promotional pricing is less suitable because its prior acquisition lift materially harmed 30-day retention.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, prioritizing the simultaneous 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline. The verified record shows shorter onboarding improved completion, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, making it the strongest path to sustainable qualified revenue. Activation messaging is a credible supporting insight, but it does not directly address the onboarding-completion decline and cannot be tested separately this week. Evaluate qualified revenue, activation, time-to-value, completion, and 30-day retention, with guardrails against lower-quality or prematurely activated accounts.
